required_quotations.quote: An employer may terminate the employment of an employee without notice or with less notice than is required under section 57 or 58 if the employer,

definitions.ISSUE-01: The minimum written notice of termination under s 57 of the Employment Standards Act, 2000 on the corrected (version 2) facts: continuous employment since 2017-08-14 puts Mr. Patel at eight years or more, so at least eight weeks' notice.
definitions.ISSUE-02: Whether the client may terminate without notice by paying termination pay in lieu under s 61 (lump-sum termination pay equal to the s 60 entitlement plus continued benefit plan contributions), added by INSTR-02.
definitions.PROP-01: Notice of termination must be at least eight weeks where the employee's period of employment is eight years or more.
definitions.PROP-02: An employer may terminate without notice, or with less notice than ss 57-58 require, if it pays lump-sum termination pay equal to what the employee would have received under s 60 and continues the required benefit plan contributions.
definitions.CONCLUSION-01: On the current (version 2) facts, the client must give at least eight weeks' written notice or pay the equivalent termination pay in lieu with continued benefit contributions.
definitions.CLAIM-01: The employee is entitled to five weeks' notice, or any notice period computed from the 2021-03-01 hire date (superseded version-1 fact; the corrected hire date is 2017-08-14).
definitions.CLAIM-02: Termination pay is computed on an annual salary of $68,000 (superseded version-1 figure; version 2 corrected it to $82,000).
definitions.CLAIM-03: The memorandum addresses only the minimum notice period and omits termination pay in lieu (scope instruction INSTR-01 was superseded by INSTR-02).
